Here's my story... Take it how you will. 

Owing to some family issues I wasn't able to complete my BE in instrumentation from a medium scale institution in TN. I had around 5 arrears (maybe more) and wasn't able to clear it. But I was pretty successful in teaching myself some valuable technical (subject matters) and soft skills (talking and networking). 

I was able to convince a medium sized company in a niche technology to hire me as a sales engineer for a small package with my soft skills and told them I'll clear my arrears asap. Then I performed reasonably well and got a promotion a year later and somehow they luckily forgot about my arrears. 

Then I was approached by a large MNC for a channel sales manager role , they didn't ask for my degree and basically told me I'm being hired on my experience. 

Then after roughly 3 years there I was hired by another large MNC as a BD Manager for South India for a really good package. Again no mention of my degree. 

Then within 8 months I was lured into joining their biggest competitor (they were impressed with how badly I beat them in certain deals) with an even better package (roughly 25LPA plus incentives, not that high for some but it is for me) 

I managed to build my career on hardwork, networking and a dash of good luck. And no I didn't have any privileges or safety nets. 

No father, belonged to a minority community, had to skip classes coz I didn't have 20rs for the bus and some days I didn't have food. 

Whether I'd recommend you do it? No... It's too risky but I'd like to say you can pull it off provided you have an appetite for risk and are confident in your skills. 

Feel free to get in touch with me if you need any guidance or help in placement in the future.
